A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LITE research, and their text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. Both end with references and contain no appendix; separately cited supplementary material is not included in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: v1 reports original Kinetics-400 and SS-V2 experiments, including token-selection comparisons, oracle analyses, model variants, and adaptive-budget results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results transferring a Kinetics-400-trained selector to UCF101, SS-V2, and AVA.

M1.justification: The Grad-CAM oracle, three-layer sigmoid MLP selector, binary cross-entropy training with frozen patch embeddings, top-token selection, and MoviNet-based adaptive budget remain unchanged. Revised explanations and transfer evaluations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds UCF101 action classification and AVA spatial-temporal action detection. Section 5.2 also introduces evaluation across dataset and task shifts using a selector trained on Kinetics-400, including transfer to the retained SS-V2 dataset.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Figure 2 and Tables 1–2 are retained. ToMe and STA labels lose configuration subscripts but retain their corresponding scores and computational costs. The new transfer experiments reuse VideoMAE as the baseline; newly cited methods are not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new transfer protocol fixes the Kinetics-400-trained selector without target-dataset training or fine-tuning and compares against target-trained VideoMAE baselines. Table 3 evaluates 90% and 70% token retention using Top-1 accuracy for classification and mAP for detection. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds substantive tests of selector generalization under dataset and task shifts. Conversely, v1's quantitative oracle-cleaning/global-branch ablations in Table 5 and the 10%-retention TimeSformer result are absent from supplied v2. v2 redirects variant results to supplementary material that is not included.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars for the experimental scores. The qualitative assertion of statistical significance for token-distribution differences is retained without a newly reported testing procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports transfer results, including SS-V2 Top-1 scores of 70.28/69.61 and AVA mAP of 31.30/30.83 at 90%/70% retention. Original Tables 1–2 and retained oracle/adaptive-budget scores are unchanged. v1's variant scores and TimeSformer 10%-retention result, 11.68 Top-1 and 29.54 Top-5, are omitted.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the formal patch-index range: v1 uses n = 1,...,N alongside a separate temporal index, although N already counts all patches; v2 separates spatial and temporal counts with N = ns × nt. The oracle mathematics is unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit claim of transfer across datasets and tasks without retraining. The contribution bullet drops the blanket architecture-agnostic and task-agnostic wording. The five principles and central efficiency contribution remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly cautions that visual-token conclusions need not extend to vision-language tokens, citing differences in contrastive alignment and token distributions. It also interprets the new transfer results as evidence that important tokens are consistent across domains. Existing Pareto, overfitting, and backbone-quality interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes implementation descriptions for edge suppression, isolated-peak removal, distribution sharpening, the global branch's 3D convolutions and self-attention, and testing MLP depth up to five layers. These become broad summaries with a supplementary-material pointer. Core input, cropping, hardware, and budget-threshold disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Six references are added, covering ActivityNet, AVA, UCF101, VLM token acceleration, token pruning for detection/segmentation, and visually grounded video question answering. The introduction adds positioning relative to vision-language research, while the existing related-work discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introduction/method passages are rewritten, the transformer review and model-variant discussion are condensed, and a zero-shot subsection is inserted. The main section order and five-principle narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 revises connections and its caption to distinguish training-only operations; several other figures receive sizing and typography changes. The transfer table is added, the variant table disappears, and retained tables and Figure 7 are rearranged. The overall two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 3 strengthen support for reusing the selector across datasets and from classification to detection, beyond v1's classification-only evidence. The visual-token scope qualification and clearer training/inference diagram also help. These gains are tempered by the loss of visible variant ablations, implementation details, and the lowest-retention TimeSformer result, yielding a limited net improvement.
